The receiver turns its open palm at the wrist, swaps to one opaque closed pose under the foreground donor grip/flower leaves, and reveals it during release. A complementary local mask opens the donor hand. One persistent rose has a stem-only grip occlusion; no full-scene pose swap, hand crossfade, synthetic skin or duplicate forearm.

wristRepair: The original donor arm remains one continuous raster piece. New hand pixels overlap only at the wrist with a curved source-crease boundary, leaving a small tone difference but no rectangular skin patch. Receiver open/closed fingers are never wiped together or alpha blended: the open palm rolls/foreshortens at its registered wrist and a single opaque pose swaps at 1.38s. Flower leaves and foreground donor fingers occlude most of that swap; a narrow closed fingertip edge remains visible above the leaf, so invisible pose replacement is not claimed. No synthetic skin, blur, color-key filter or duplicate forearm.
